epics.title: Slice one: migrate the memory
epics.rationale: Proposed as one epic and approved. The platform stories and the migration stories are one system, neither half ships alone, and the epic's definition of done is the empty diff, which needs every story. Risk profile is the one test that argued for a split, and it would have produced two epics that must both finish before either is useful.

tasks.title: Provision PostgreSQL with pgvector on amaterasu

docImpact.note: docs/runbooks/postgres-setup.md records the twelve tuning settings and where each number came from. They are scaled from nabium's postgres-tuning.md rather than copied, because that runbook targets a 32 GB host and amaterasu holds 7.6 GB shared with NFS.

The stock unit orders After=network.target, which is not enough when listen_addresses names an address: the address may not be up yet. A drop-in orders Postgres after network-online.target, and scripts/provision-amaterasu-root.sh writes it.

tasks.title: Scaffold the repository and migration tooling

docImpact.note: The README gains a Running it section: the clean-clone steps, the five npm commands, and how to write a migration file. Extended, not replaced.
Node 22.18 strips types on load, so the repository needs no bundler and no build step. npm run build type-checks and emits nothing. Tests run on node --test.

libpq and node-postgres read sslmode=require two different ways. connect() translates it to the driver's no-verify, so one .env serves psql and Node. amaterasu's certificate is self-signed, so no client can verify the chain.
The runner refuses rather than guesses: a populated database stops it, and so does a second up with nothing to apply. REQ-007 asks for this instead of idempotence.

tasks.title: Create the core schema

docImpact.note: ADR-0007 records the nodes registry: why edges need real foreign keys, the two alternatives rejected, and that the three constraints cover different directions. The deferred trigger exists because the foreign keys cannot see a node with no child row.
docs/schema.md explains all ten tables, the five enums, and three decisions a reader would question.
facts.path is a schema gap the PRD's column list missed. A wikilink resolves against a note's file name and title is prose, so without path nothing can turn [[a-note]] back into a row.

sources/ notes carry a different frontmatter set entirely: thirteen keys with almost no overlap with the spaces. Not a gap: sources.body stores the file verbatim, so the mapping test reads the four space directories only.
The embedding model is voyage-4 at 1024 dimensions, checked against Voyage's model list on 27 August 2026. The brief names voyage-3, which is now legacy. Changing either value is a migration.
A machine never marking its own work verified is now a check constraint rather than a prompt instruction. The policy's hardest rule, enforced by the database.

tasks.title: Read and validate the vault's markdown
Turn wikilinks into typed edges
Turn inline tasks into rows
Implement the four gates as tested code

docImpact.note: Every model call passes through src/memory/inference.ts. Only a recorded implementation exists, so the suite passes with no network and CI needs no credential. A live one plugs in there when the ingesting slice needs it.

A gate's prompt is a file under src/memory/prompts/, read on every call. A renamed prompt throws and rejects rather than judging by a stale instruction. Proved by moving one away and watching the suite fail with ENOENT.
The default is to reject, four ways over: a hedge, a refusal, an empty answer and a verdict wrapped in prose all read as errors, and an error rejects. So does a gate that throws.

Gate 3 matches on the title, case-insensitively. It catches a duplicate and passes a candidate that merely mentions the same entity. It will not catch a duplicate worded differently: compare embeddings once KPA-12 fills them.

tasks.title: Reach amaterasu's Postgres from the Mac over TLS

docImpact.note: ADR-0008 records that the migration runs on the Mac and writes to amaterasu. Three rejected options and four consequences. Running it on amaterasu loses, because the vault and check.py cannot move and check.py's report is the verification oracle.
connect() refuses any sslmode that does not encrypt. prefer is the one worth naming: it falls back to plain text without saying so.

libpq and node-postgres read sslmode=require two different ways. libpq encrypts without verifying, the driver verifies and fails on amaterasu's self-signed certificate. connect() translates require to no-verify so one .env serves psql and Node.

tasks.title: Keep every secret out of the repository and out of the unit file

docImpact.note: Real values moved from the repository's .env to ~/.config/kpa/env, mode 0600 in a 0700 directory. The repository holds no .env at all now, so anything in another session that reads one finds nothing.
gitleaks' default rules do not flag a database URL carrying a password. Proved by scanning a commit that held one. scripts/scan-history.sh therefore runs three checks, not one.
Node's --env-file does not overwrite a variable already exported. CI can set DATABASE_URL_TEST directly and carry no file, and a stale exported variable silently beats an edited file.
The systemd EnvironmentFile= section of the runbook is written but not run: no unit exists yet. It is marked as a pattern rather than a checked procedure.

tasks.title: Run the checks on every push, and record the repository's conventions

docImpact.note: CLAUDE.md's placeholder section is filled in: the commands, the two databases, the layout, and the commit rules. Lines 1 to 38 are untouched, so the push-straight-to-main decision survives byte for byte.
CI pins pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg18, the same two versions amaterasu runs, so a green run cannot come from a server the box does not have.

connect() now lets a loopback host connect in the clear. Not a concession to CI: the worker will run on amaterasu where Postgres also listens on 127.0.0.1, and TLS over loopback buys nothing. Every remote host must still encrypt.

CI found a real defect on its first run: the TLS test asserted pg_stat_ssl.ssl unconditionally, which contradicted the loopback exception the same commit added. Fixed in 11c4d79. No local run could have found it, because every local run uses a remote host.
